EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026

EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: There is no target-role headline or summary.
items.because: A reader has to infer the quant-research direction from the experience section.

items.says: The current retail role receives more prominence than the research qualifications.
items.because: It is the first experience entry but is outside the inferred target field.

items.says: Replace the phone number, email address and portfolio link if they are literal placeholders.
items.because: The 555 number and example.com address look like sample data.

items.says: Clarify whether the Assistant Store Manager role is part-time and how it fits alongside the Ph.D. and research work.
items.because: The current dates invite questions about workload and chronology.

items.says: Specify what “within budget” means and how it was measured.
items.because: The result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Give the measurement period and say whether the reduction was sustained.
items.because: The percentage needs context.

items.says: Define “risk-adjusted returns,” the comparison, costs and evaluation period, and its relationship to the later Sharpe claim.
items.because: The 35% improvement is otherwise hard to interpret.

items.says: Make the description of the splits and embargo precise and defensible.
items.because: The bullet claims point-in-time evaluation.

items.says: Add more evidence of the feature store’s scope or impact if supportable.
items.because: Reuse in two later signal projects is a good start.

items.says: Distinguish approval for a future allocation from implementation or realized performance.
items.because: The wording establishes approval, not that the allocation went live.

items.says: The best of 400 backtested configurations is reported as expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the best result creates selection bias and does not by itself estimate live performance.

items.says: Move the signal result higher within the internship entry.
items.because: The strongest, clearest quant result is buried.

items.says: Clarify how this signal relates to the 35% result and the Kaggle claim.
items.because: The claims may describe overlapping work or results.

items.says: The Monte Carlo runs used the same random seed on every worker.
items.because: Identical seeds can produce identical or correlated streams, invalidating the intended independent simulations.

items.says: Be ready to substantiate the log-factor comparison and your role in the proof.
Give research, modeling and software evidence priority over the teaching bullet if space is limited.
items.because: Teaching is less relevant to quant research.

items.says: Make the data period and evaluation design easy to identify.
items.because: They provide context for the out-of-sample forecast result.

items.says: Clarify how dependence across indices and crisis-period comparisons were handled.
items.because: Those details matter to the stated significance results.

items.says: Label the working paper without implying publication or peer-reviewed acceptance.
items.because: A seminar presentation is not either of those.

items.says: Add a result, competition standing or specific contribution.
items.because: The bullet names activities but is too generic.

items.says: Identify the leakage and explain how time-grouped folds corrected it.
items.because: A smaller validation-to-leaderboard gap does not on its own establish reduced leakage.

items.says: Distinguish this signal’s work, ownership and result from the Northpeak claim, or avoid claiming the same achievement twice.
items.because: The signal, test duration and performance metric closely match the internship claim.

items.says: Connect Kafka to substantive experience or reconsider listing it.
items.because: It appears in skills but not in the experience or projects.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
Make relevant methods easier to scan, listing only ones you can defend.
items.because: The Methods list is brief relative to the detailed evidence elsewhere.
